correctness_confidence.basis: Theorems 3.1, 4.3 and 5.1 follow from valid self-adjoint power estimates; both the continuous-cutoff proof and the new paper-level dyadic proof withstand direct checking. The zero-rate and zero-time cases are handled correctly. No counterexample satisfying the stated hypotheses was found. Confidence in the formal build is limited to source inspection and historical evidence, not a new Lean run.

rigor.basis: The order of quantifiers permits arbitrary finite constants per observable while keeping one rate. The supplied Lean statements preserve self-adjointness, completeness, density of the span and rate nonnegativity. The bridge uses even positive times and enlarges the orbit constant to cover n=0. Theorem 5.2 correctly gives a common contraction exponent without claiming an unconstructed Hamiltonian.

novelty.basis: The operator criterion is classical spectral-theoretic mathematics and now also has a short elementary proof in the paper. The contribution is its explicit Lean implementation and packaging for observable families. Neither mathematical priority nor priority of mechanization has been established by an exhaustive comparison.

significance.basis: This is a useful, bounded formalization contribution clarifying that support-dependent prefactors do not defeat a common-rate dense-family argument. It supplies no concrete gauge-theory state space, density theorem, correlator identification, volume limit or continuum mass gap, as the manuscript expressly acknowledges.

reproducibility.basis: The PDF hash and all six manifest entries match. The two supplied formal modules allow substantive statement/proof inspection, and the historical transcript contains the named central declarations with only the listed foundational axioms. Its 2304 answers, including 22 empty dependency sets, were independently recounted. The supplied material is not a complete dependency checkout: TransferGap.lean, the pinned library and the build driver were not available within the permitted packet, and no new Lean compilation or replay was performed.

summary: I recommend acceptance of this exact nine-page PDF as a modest formalization and exposition paper, with a Millennium score of 3.30 rather than a score reflecting progress on Yang--Mills. The dense-family theorem is correct: self-adjointness converts a common exponential orbit rate into the pointwise bound ||Sv|| <= r||v||, after which density gives the operator norm bound. The connected-correlator bridge correctly excludes n=0 from the structural identity and handles that term separately. The new dyadic proof removes any mathematical need for functional calculus while accurately remaining outside the preserved Lean declarations. The supplied formal sources support the central complex statements, and the historical oracle counts agree with the manuscript; this is not independent certification of a fresh build. Astra's prior participation is disclosed as involved_in_manuscript. I found no unresolved material objection invalidating a main result. This recommendation is a model assessment, not a human editorial decision or publication authorization.
strengths: The dyadic inequality on page 4 is valid over both real and complex Hilbert spaces, including a separate r=0 argument, and makes the role of arbitrary prefactors especially transparent.
The continuous-cutoff factorization uses a strictly positive denominator and is valid at zero and at the cutoff boundary; the supplied Lean proof implements the same argument.
The source mem_decayDomain_of_connCorrC supplies max(sqrt(max(C,0)), ||v||), correctly covering n=0 even for a pure-vacuum vector with vanishing connected correlator.
The backward-shift example correctly identifies why self-adjointness cannot simply be removed, while the text distinguishes strong decay from decay at a common exponential rate.
The manuscript clearly separates its abstract operator results from a gauge-theory application and separates a contraction exponent from a Hamiltonian mass bound.
weaknesses: The abstract's phrase 'All results are machine-checked' is broader than the later explicit treatment of the dyadic argument and counterexamples as paper-level additions. 'The mapped main theorems are machine-checked' would be a clearer optional wording; the body makes the actual boundary sufficiently explicit.

The preserved DenseClustering.lean docstring still says that functional calculus is mathematically necessary. That historical comment is contradicted by the valid new dyadic proof. It should remain identified as superseded historical exposition wherever those sources are presented; it does not alter the declarations or invalidate their proofs.

The independent reproduction available in this review is partial. The full pinned checkout and build were not replayed, and the historical transcript alone cannot certify the current source-to-build relationship or exhaustive dependency coverage.

The prior-art discussion remains broad. The publisher records support the bibliographic references and the transfer-positivity attribution, but this review did not establish an exact antecedent theorem or verify the cited Glimm--Jaffe section. The modest novelty claim is appropriate.
